title: Open/Closed Principle
description: Learn to write code that is open for extension but closed for modification.

data.text: The **Open/Closed Principle (OCP)** states that software entities (classes, modules, functions) should be open for extension but closed for modification.

Rather than modifying existing, working code to add new behavior, you should extend the code through inheritance, composition, or interfaces. This reduces the risk of introducing bugs in existing functionality.

data.title: Violating OCP

data.text: Adding a new customer type requires modifying this class, which violates OCP.

data.title: Following OCP
Key Takeaways
points: Use interfaces and abstractions to enable extension
New functionality is added by creating new classes, not modifying existing ones
Strategy pattern is a common way to achieve OCP
data.takeaway: Design your code so that new features can be added with minimal changes to existing code.
